title: The lowest-fat cheeses

seo.title: Lowest-fat cheeses: ranking per 100 grams
seo.meta_description: 1% cottage cheese and part-skim ricotta contain far less fat than part-skim mozzarella, feta or cheddar. Compare representative USDA values per 100 g.
seo.search_intent: Compare cheeses by total fat on an equal 100-g basis and understand how moisture and milkfat affect the result.

excerpt: Fresh, reduced-fat cheeses dominate the low-fat end. USDA references put 1% cottage cheese at about 1 g fat/100 g and part-skim ricotta at 7.9 g, compared with 15.9 g for part-skim mozzarella, 21.3 g for feta and roughly 33 g for cheddar. Product labels still matter because recipes vary.
content_html:
“Cheese” ranges from very moist fresh products to dense aged cheeses. A fair fat comparison uses grams of fat per 100 g and a clearly defined cheese type.

Representative values per 100 g

CheeseTotal fatApprox. calories
1% lowfat cottage cheese~1.0 g~72
Part-skim ricotta~7.9 g~138
Part-skim mozzarella~15.9 g~254
Feta~21.3 g~264
Cheddar~33 g~400

These are specific USDA references. Fat-free cottage cheese, fresh mozzarella and reduced-fat branded products can differ substantially, so the package label should override a category average.

Water dilutes fat per 100 g

The 1% cottage-cheese reference is roughly 82–83% water. Aged cheese has lost much more water, concentrating fat, protein, calcium and calories into the same 100-g weight.

Milkfat level matters too

Part-skim ricotta at 7.9 g fat contains about 8 g less fat per 100 g than part-skim mozzarella at 15.9 g and about 25 g less than cheddar near 33 g.

Low fat does not mean low sodium

A USDA 1% cottage reference contains about 406 mg sodium/100 g, while a no-salt-added version is near 13 mg. Fat and sodium have to be checked separately.

Serving size changes the practical result

Thirty grams of cheddar at 33 g fat/100 g provide about 9.9 g fat. A full 100 g of 1% cottage cheese provides about 1 g. Typical serving sizes differ greatly among cheese styles.

Moist, reduced-fat fresh cheeses—especially cottage cheese and lower-fat ricotta—sit at the low-fat end. Water content and starting milkfat explain much of the ranking.

faq.question: What cheese has the least fat?
faq.answer: Among common references, 1% cottage cheese can contain about 1 g fat per 100 g, far below aged cheeses.

faq.question: Is ricotta low in fat?
faq.answer: Part-skim ricotta provides about 7.9 g/100 g, lower than part-skim mozzarella (~15.9 g) or feta (~21.3 g).

faq.question: Does low-fat cheese mean low sodium?
faq.answer: No. Fat and sodium are independent; check both values on the nutrition label.
